source.title: Multiplication Beyond Groups: Stratified Fourier Mechanisms in Transformer Circuits
source.authors: Z. Chen; Junaidi Hasan; Akhil Srinivasan; Hemkesh Bandi; J. Alper

record.tranche_reason: The study trains a small transformer on an algorithmic modular-arithmetic task and reports training and held-out accuracy over time, directly measuring the grokking pattern in a new multiplication setting.
record.gate_note: The accuracy trajectory in Appendix B, Figure 5 bears on V1. The paper also discusses grokking and analyzes learned representations, but its static analyses do not track gradual circuit formation or show that progress measures anticipate an accuracy jump. The use of AdamW and weight decay is not an optimizer or weight-norm comparison. Other cited grokking results are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study trains the Nanda et al. one-layer transformer on modular multiplication (n=165, 30% of pairs, AdamW with weight decay 1). It reports train and validation accuracy over 25,000 epochs, with a grokking gap before validation accuracy catches up (Appendix B, Fig. 5). This bears directly on the first part of V1. The paper's main contribution is a static mechanistic analysis, which tests no other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that the model groks and that its embeddings, attention, MLP and logits fit a stratified, local-Fourier 'Monoid Extension' of GCR. They describe this evidence as correlational and leave progress measures for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a related small-transformer algorithmic training setup and accuracy trajectory, but studies modular multiplication over composite moduli; the reported grokking curve is for n=165 and one seed, without a training-set-size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The main grokking trajectory is reported for n=165 and seed 1 only. In the stability analyses, exact Fourier peak locations vary across seeds while the coarse block structure is described as consistent.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 10 seeds and four moduli, the coarse J-class block structure is stable in embeddings, attention and MLP activations, but exact Fourier peak locations vary. Table 5 gives PCA dimensionality of about 10 ± 0.6–1.7 components.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coarse representational structure is seed-stable while the specific Fourier frequencies chosen vary across seeds. This is a representation-level stability measure, not algorithm identification across architectures or hyperparameters.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning
record.problems: The grokking trajectory is presented as a plot without numeric accuracy or timing values or uncertainty, and the main result is reported for one seed and one training-data fraction. The authors state that their mechanistic evidence is correlational and that causal interventions remain future work.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks. Only one training fraction (30%) is used.
All parts. The circuit analysis is static at the end of training; progress measures are left as future work.
All parts. No non-algorithmic data and no sweep of initialization scale or weight norm.
All parts. No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
All parts. Weight decay is fixed at 1; no critical dataset size and no ungrokking test.
No identification and comparison of algorithms across architectures or hyperparameters. The seed-stability results are representational only.
All parts. No optimizer or numerical controls.

missing.what: MLP-only architecture stated to generalize faster than the transformer. No curve or timing is reported, and it is unclear whether it shows a delay.

record.verdict_notes: Grokking is reported only in passing, through a single figure caption and a conclusion remark. The mechanistic results are end-of-training snapshots and do not bear on V2's timing claims. AdamW with weight decay is fixed, not varied, so V5 and V7 are untested.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports one training-set fraction and does not test whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks. It gives no numeric timing or accuracy values for the trajectory.
No time-resolved circuit or progress measure is tested for whether it anticipates the generalization jump.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm comparison is tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
The study does not test whether weight decay favors a more efficient circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Seed stability of some representation patterns is reported, but the study does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs.
No optimizer-instability or floating-point/softmax control is tested.
